findings.highlight: the ground is strewn with rubble.
findings.evidenceJa: 荒野のようだった地上は、瓦礫の山になりつつある。
findings.governingReading: The formerly wasteland-like ground is becoming a mountain of rubble.
findings.explanation: The English removes both the former wasteland image and the growing mountain scale.

findings.highlight: people can’t live without oxygen
findings.evidenceJa: 酸素をとりこまないと人間は動けない
findings.governingReading: Humans cannot move unless they take in oxygen.
findings.explanation: A local mechanical reason for forced breathing becomes a general biological truism about survival.

findings.highlight: I would stop moving soon.
findings.evidenceJa: もうじき動けなくな
findings.governingReading: Shirou’s thought breaks off as he reaches becoming unable to move soon.
findings.explanation: The English supplies a completed conditional statement where the source visibly fails mid-word.

findings.highlight: I am the bone of my sword.
findings.evidenceJa: 体は剣で出来ている。
findings.governingReading: The narration directly states that Shirou’s body is made of swords.
findings.explanation: A familiar incantation line replaces the literal statement about his current body.

findings.highlight: In front of the crater, the Great Holy Grail.
findings.evidenceJa: 大聖杯と呼ばれるクレーターの前。
findings.governingReading: He reaches the crater called the Greater Grail.
findings.explanation: The English splits the name relation into a malformed apposition that can make the crater and Grail seem separate.

findings.highlight: Bathed in the ruddy glow
findings.evidenceJa: 赤黒い炎に照らされて
findings.governingReading: The figure is illuminated by red-black flames.
findings.explanation: The English removes both the black component and the flames themselves.

findings.highlight: He’ll smash my head if I show such an opening.
findings.evidenceJa: セイバーの剣を作る前に頭蓋を砕かれている。
findings.governingReading: Kirei would crush Shirou’s skull before Shirou could make Saber’s sword.
findings.explanation: The English removes the scene’s identification of the intended final projected weapon.

findings.highlight: Good and evil mean nothing to me now.
findings.evidenceJa: ……そんなもの、答えられる筈がない。
findings.governingReading: Shirou says he cannot possibly answer such a question.
findings.explanation: The English deletes the bridge between Kirei’s question and Shirou’s loss of his former justice.

findings.highlight: it’s up to you to decide which is which.
findings.evidenceJa: その属性を分けるのはあくまで自身の選択による。
findings.governingReading: A person’s own choices determine which moral attribute they incline toward.
findings.explanation: The English makes the choice classify good and evil themselves rather than shape the chooser’s moral direction.

findings.highlight: rare moments of goodwill shown by evil men
findings.evidenceJa: 悪人が、戯れに見せる善意
findings.governingReading: An evil person may display goodwill capriciously or as play.
findings.explanation: The English invents rarity and removes the unsettling playful motive.

findings.highlight: There is no existence that is born as evil, that is unwanted by everyone.
findings.evidenceJa: 何者にも望まれぬモノ、生まれながらに悪であるモノなどない。
findings.governingReading: Nothing is wholly unwanted by all, and nothing is born evil.
findings.explanation: The English tangles two coordinated denials into an ambiguous relative clause.

findings.highlight: “all evils of this world”
findings.evidenceJa: 人間が望みあげてしまった“全ての悪”
findings.governingReading: Human wishing has collectively raised or fashioned “all the world’s evil.”
findings.explanation: The English omits human responsibility for producing the entity Kirei would forgive.

findings.highlight: a pure deity that people made
findings.evidenceJa: 悪しか持たぬ、人々が創り上げた純粋な単一神
findings.governingReading: A pure, singular god made by people possesses nothing but evil.
findings.explanation: The English removes singularity and the defining restriction to evil alone.

findings.highlight: What Angra Mainyu thinks about his own actions
findings.evidenceJa: 自分をどう思うか
findings.governingReading: The question is what the entity thinks of itself.
findings.explanation: The English redirects self-judgment toward evaluation of its actions.

findings.highlight: emotions like those of humans
findings.evidenceJa: 人に近い意思
findings.governingReading: The entity may possess a will or intention resembling a human being’s.
findings.explanation: The English substitutes emotions for will, changing the faculty Kirei makes morally relevant.

findings.highlight: agonizes over its doings
findings.evidenceJa: 自らの存在を嘆く
findings.governingReading: It laments its own existence.
findings.explanation: The English changes existential self-rejection into regret over actions.

findings.highlight: Those with defects at birth.
findings.evidenceJa: 生まれながらにして持ち得ぬもの。
findings.governingReading: Something it cannot possess from birth.
findings.explanation: The English invents people with congenital defects, shifting a missing possession into bodily defect.

findings.highlight: when you are different from others
findings.evidenceJa: 外界との隔たりをもったモノ
findings.governingReading: A being cut off from the external world continues living alone.
findings.explanation: The English turns radical isolation from the outside world into ordinary interpersonal difference.

findings.highlight: I shake off the vagueness
findings.evidenceJa: おぼろがかった視界を振り絞って
findings.governingReading: Shirou strains his dim and hazy vision to glare at Kirei.
findings.explanation: The English implies he clears an abstract vagueness rather than forcing failing eyesight to function.

findings.highlight: no regret or doubts
findings.evidenceJa: 後悔も間違いもない
findings.governingReading: Kirei speaks as though he has neither regret nor error.
findings.explanation: Doubts changes denial of having been mistaken into psychological certainty.

findings.highlight: because I didn’t want to accept the fact
findings.evidenceJa: 最後まで気付かないままでいる為に
findings.governingReading: Shirou made Kirei an enemy so he could remain unaware of liking him until the end.
findings.explanation: The English removes the deliberate lifelong or final avoidance of recognition.

findings.highlight: he doesn’t know any other way to live.
findings.evidenceJa: 本当に正しい生き方を知らないだけ。
findings.governingReading: Kirei knows no other way of living that is truly right.
findings.explanation: The English removes Shirou’s morally loaded qualification of the unavailable alternative.

findings.highlight: Many things slipped out between my fingers
findings.evidenceJa: 指の隙間から零れ落ちた無数の澱
findings.governingReading: Countless dregs or accumulated sediment slipped through Kirei’s fingers despite every discipline.
findings.explanation: The English replaces the image of accumulated residue with unspecified things.

findings.highlight: at a speed he can’t avoid
findings.evidenceJa: 躱しようのないタイミングで
findings.governingReading: Shirou attacks at a moment whose timing makes evasion impossible.
findings.explanation: The English transfers inevitability from timing to speed.

findings.highlight: It tries to damage the inside instead of outside.
findings.evidenceJa: 外部はもとより内部へのダメージ
findings.governingReading: The art accounts for internal damage in addition to external damage.
findings.explanation: The English replaces inclusion with opposition and excludes external damage.

findings.highlight: without much in it
findings.evidenceJa: 内に何も宿らぬ物
findings.governingReading: Kirei’s imitation contains nothing within it.
findings.explanation: The English weakens categorical emptiness into merely lacking much.

findings.highlight: is getting ready for the explosion.
findings.evidenceJa: 一秒後の爆発に備えている。
findings.governingReading: Kirei’s trained body prepares for an explosive release one second later.
findings.explanation: The English removes the exact immediate timing.

findings.highlight: a battle with your body at stake
findings.evidenceJa: 自身を賭ける戦い
findings.governingReading: The fight stakes the combatants’ selves.
findings.explanation: The English narrows existential selfhood to the physical body.

findings.highlight: some centuries-old wish
findings.evidenceJa: 何百年と続いた妄執
findings.governingReading: The centuries-long fixation is an obsessive delusion or tenacity.
findings.explanation: Wish sanitizes the pathological obsession driving the ritual.

findings.highlight: the end of this small world
findings.evidenceJa: 一つの世界の崩壊
findings.governingReading: The collapse of one world is irrelevant to Shirou in this moment.
findings.explanation: The English adds small, reducing the scale without source support.
